chunks: Many faces will be joyous on that day,

key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: On that day (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for faces to be 'joyous' on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often contrasted with the 'ashkhat' (humbled faces) of the wicked, emphasizing that the radiance of the righteous stems from the light of divine knowledge and adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt. The term 'na'imah' implies not just fleeting joy but a sustained state of bliss rooted in the eternal covenant of walayah. This duality serves as a practical reminder for believers to cultivate inner serenity through consistent devotion and spiritual purity.
